items.title: Russia downs over 1,400 Ukrainian drones as Kyiv hits a key bridge in Crimea
items.description: Ukraine's forces targeted a key rail and road bridge between Russia and the Crimean Peninsula for a second day. Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv.

items.description: Tuesday’s closure on the bridge came less than a day after traffic resumed following a drone attack that shut the crossing for more than 16 hours.

items.title: From Russia's Infamous Gold-Mining Region, A Ready Supply Of Men For Ukraine War
items.description: Before he signed up to fight in Ukraine, Denis Dmitriyev served time for robbing another gold-mining laborer in Kolyma. He is one of at least 20 men from the legendarily harsh Russian gold-mining region in war who have been killed in the war. Nearly all were convicted criminals or chronic debtors.

items.title: French troops are now operating in Ukraine
items.description: Small contingents of French military personnel are carrying out rotations in Ukraine to provide training and repair military equipment, a source close to the matter confirmed to Le Monde, following a report by RFI.

items.title: ASEAN offers Myanmar's sidelined leaders a path back to summits, but says restrictions will stay until there is meaningful progress on its peace plan
items.description: Southeast Asian leaders have agreed to engage Myanmar in stages after years of excluding its leaders from high-level meetings. The bloc says Myanmar could regain full representation if it makes progress on a peace plan.

items.title: First Person: Managing risk on Ukraine’s frontline
items.description: Humanitarian workers providing support to communities on the frontline of the war between Ukraine and Russia must balance remaining close to those in need with the heightened risks of operating in a conflict zone, according to the top UN official in Ukraine.
